chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fazl ibn Uthman al-Muradi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Four [characteristics]; whoever possesses them, destruction will not be upon Allah's decree upon him after these, except for one who destroys himself.'
The servant intends a good deed and performs it; if he does not perform it, Allah writes for him one good deed due to his good intention, and if he performs it, Allah writes for him ten [good deeds].
And he intends an evil deed to perform; if he does not perform it, nothing is written against him, and if he performs it, it is postponed for seven hours.
And the Companion of Good Deeds says to the Companion of Evil Deeds, and he is the Companion of the Left: 'Do not be hasty; perhaps he will follow it with a good deed that will erase it.'
Surely good deeds take away evil deeds.

If he says: 'I seek forgiveness of Allah, who is no god except He, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Mighty, the Wise, the Forgiving, the Merciful, the Lord of Majesty and Generosity,' and repents to Him, nothing is written against him.
And if seven hours pass and he does not follow it with a good deed and seeking forgiveness,
The Companion of Good Deeds says to the Companion of Evil Deeds: 'Write [it] against the wretched, the deprived one.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الشِّمَالِ: Companion of the Left (Angel recording evil)

ai.seo_question: How are good and evil deeds recorded based on intention and action in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the Shia concept of divine mercy in the accounting of deeds, emphasizing that intention alone carries weight even before action. It highlights the unique 'seven-hour' grace period for evil intentions, allowing time for repentance or a counterbalancing good deed, a mechanism rooted in the Quranic promise that 'good deeds erase bad ones.' This reflects the scholarly view of Allah as both Just and Merciful, where the 'Scribe of Good Deeds' delays the 'Scribe of Evil Deeds' to offer the believer a chance for redemption.
